nodes.name: Compressed sensing
nodes.statement: \textit{Compressed (or compressive) sensing} (CS) is a technique for recovering a high-dimensional signal from lower-dimensional data, whose components represent partial information about the signal, by utilizing prior knowledge on the sparsity of the signal \cite{CandesWakin2008}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.genus: a technique for recovering a high-dimensional signal from lower-dimensional data
differentia: by utilizing prior knowledge on the sparsity of the signal

nodes.name: Standard linear CS measurement model
nodes.statement: Let us suppose a situation that an $N$-dimensional vector $\textrm{\boldmath $x^{0}$}$ is linearly transformed into an $M$-dimensional vector $\textrm{\boldmath $y$}$ by an $M \times N$ measurement matrix $\boldmath \Phi$, where $\textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Unique exact recovery of sparse signals with incoherent measurements
nodes.statement: However, when the $N$-dimensional signal is guaranteed to have only $K<M$ nonzero entries in some convenient basis and the measurement matrix is {incoherent} with that basis, there is a high probability that the inverse problem has a unique and exact solution.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: the $N$-dimensional signal is guaranteed to have only $K<M$ nonzero entries in some convenient basis
the measurement matrix is {incoherent} with that basis
conclusions: there is a high probability that the inverse problem has a unique and exact solution
nodes.statement_short: A $K$-sparse signal ($K<M$) measured by an incoherent matrix is, with high probability, uniquely and exactly recoverable.

nodes.name: 1-bit compressed sensing
nodes.statement: Addressing the practical relevance of CS in such operation, Boufounos and Baraniuk recently proposed and examined a CS scheme, often called {\em 1-bit compressed sensing (1-bit CS)}, in which the signal is recovered from only the sign data of the linear measurements $\textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\mathrm{sign}\left(\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$}\right)$, where $\mathrm{sign}(x)=x/|x|$ for $x \ne 0$ operates for vectors in the component-wise manner \cite{1bitCS}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
differentia: the signal is recovered from only the sign data of the linear measurements $\textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\mathrm{sign}\left(\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$}\right)$
nodes.statement_short: 1-bit CS recovers the signal from only the signs of the linear measurements.

nodes.name: Sparse signal prior
nodes.statement: Let us suppose that entry $x_i^0$ $(i=1,2,\ldots,N)$ of $N$-dimensional signal (vector) $\vm{x}^0 \in \mathbb{R}^N$ is independently generated from an identical sparse distribution: \begin{equation} P\left(x\right)=\left(1-\rho\right) \delta \left( x \right) + \rho \tilde{P} \left( x \right), \end{equation} where $\rho \in [0,1]$ represents the density of nonzero entries in the signal and $\tilde{P} (x)$ is a distribution function of $x \in \mathbb{R}$ that does not have finite mass at $x=0$.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Signal entries are i.i.d. from a Bernoulli-mixture prior with nonzero density $\rho$ and nonzero part $\tilde P$.

nodes.name: 1-bit measurement model with Gaussian matrix
nodes.statement: In 1-bit CS the measurement is performed as \begin{equation} \textrm{\boldmath $y$}=\mathrm{sign} \left( \textrm{\boldmath $\Phi x^{0}$} \right), \end{equation} where for simplicity we assume that each entry of $M \times N$ measurement matrix $\vm{\Phi}$ is provided as an independent sample from an identical Gaussian distribution of zero mean and variance $N^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Measurements are signs of $\Phi x^0$, with i.i.d. Gaussian $\Phi$ entries of variance $1/N$.

nodes.name: l1-based 1-bit CS recovery problem
nodes.statement: Given $\vm{y}$ and $\vm{\Phi}$, the signal reconstruction is carried out by searching for a sparse vector $\vm{x} =(x_i) \in \mathbb{R}^N$ under the constraint of ${\rm sign}\left (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x} \right )=\vm{y}$. For this task the authors of \cite{1bitCS} proposed a scheme of \begin{eqnarray} \mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{x} } \left \{||\vm{x}||_1 \right \} \ {\rm subj. \ to} \ {\rm sign}\left (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x} \right )=\vm{y} \ {\rm and} \ ||\vm{x}||_2=\sqrt{N}, \end{eqnarray} based on the $l_1$-recovery method widely used and studied for standard CS problems \cite{CandesWakin2008}. Here $|| \vm{x}||_1 =\sum_{i=1}^N |x_i|$ and $||\vm{x}||_2=|\vm{x}|=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^2}$ denote the $l_1$- and $l_2$-norms of $\vm{x}$, respectively.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Minimise $\|x\|_1$ subject to sign consistency with $y$ and the sphere constraint $\|x\|_2=\sqrt N$.

nodes.name: Sign measurements erase signal length
nodes.statement: The measurement process of (\ref{measurement}) completely erases the information of length $|\vm{x}^0|$, which makes it impossible to recover the signal uniquely.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup

nodes.name: Normalized recovered signal and recovery success
nodes.statement: We therefore introduce an extra normalization constraint $|\hat{\vm{x}}|=\sqrt{N}$ for the recovered signal $\hat{\vm{x}}$, and we consider the recovery successful when the direction cosine ${\vm{x}}^0 \cdot \hat{\vm{x}}/(|\vm{x}^0| |\hat{\vm{x}}|)$ is sufficiently large.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: The recovered signal $\hat x$ is normalised to length $\sqrt N$; recovery is judged by the direction cosine with $x^0$.

nodes.name: Non-convexity of the 1-bit l1 recovery problem
nodes.statement: Unlike the standard CS problem, finding a solution of (\ref{l1recovery}) is non-trivial because the norm constraint $|{\vm{x}}|=\sqrt{N}$ keeps it from being a convex optimization problem (Figures \ref{Normal_vs_1bit} (a) and (b)).
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup

nodes.name: Renormalized Fixed Point Iteration (RFPI)
nodes.statement: 1)\ \mbox{\bf Initialization}:\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Seed}: \hspace{80pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\ \text{s.t}\ ||\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}||_{2}=\sqrt{N},\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Descent step size}:\hspace{13pt}\delta\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Counter}: \hspace{62pt} k\GETS 0\\ 2)\ \mbox{\bf Counter\ Increase}:\\ \hspace{30pt}k \GETS k+1\\ 3)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}\GETS (\textsc{Y}\Phi)^{\rm T} f^\prime (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1})\\ 4)\ \mbox{\bf Gradient projection on sphere surface}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\GETS \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}-\langle \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}, \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}\rangle\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}/N\\ 5)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{h}\GETS \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}-\delta\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\\ 6)\ \mbox{\bf Shrinkage ($l_1$-gradient descent)}:\\ \hspace{30pt}(\mathbf{u})_i\GETS\text{sign}((\mathbf{h})_{i})\text{max}\{|(\mathbf{h})_i|-\frac{\delta}{\lambda},0\} \ \text{for all}\ i \\ 7)\ \mbox{\bf Normalization}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k}\GETS \sqrt{N} \frac{\mathbf{u}}{||\mathbf{u}||_2}\\ 8)\ \bold{Iteration}: \mbox{Repeat from 2) until convergence.}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Inner loop of RFPI: one-sided quadratic gradient step projected on the sphere, $l_1$ shrinkage, then renormalisation to $\sqrt N$, repeated to convergence.

nodes.name: Initialization
nodes.statement: 1)\ \mbox{\bf Initialization}:\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Seed}: \hspace{80pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\ \text{s.t}\ ||\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0}||_{2}=\sqrt{N},\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Descent step size}:\hspace{13pt}\delta\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Counter}: \hspace{62pt} k\GETS 0\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Seed on the sphere, set step size and counter

nodes.name: Counter increase
nodes.statement: 2)\ \mbox{\bf Counter\ Increase}:\\ \hspace{30pt}k \GETS k+1\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup

nodes.name: One-sided quadratic gradient
nodes.statement: 3)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}\GETS (\textsc{Y}\Phi)^{\rm T} f^\prime (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1})\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Gradient of the one-sided quadratic sign-consistency penalty

nodes.name: Gradient projection on sphere surface
nodes.statement: 4)\ \mbox{\bf Gradient projection on sphere surface}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\GETS \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}-\langle \mathbf{\overline{f}}_{k}, \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}\rangle\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}/N\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Project the gradient onto the tangent space of the sphere

nodes.name: One-sided quadratic gradient descent
nodes.statement: 5)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{h}\GETS \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}-\delta\mathbf{\tilde{f}}_{k}\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Gradient step of size $\delta$

nodes.name: Shrinkage
nodes.statement: 6)\ \mbox{\bf Shrinkage ($l_1$-gradient descent)}:\\ \hspace{30pt}(\mathbf{u})_i\GETS\text{sign}((\mathbf{h})_{i})\text{max}\{|(\mathbf{h})_i|-\frac{\delta}{\lambda},0\} \ \text{for all}\ i \\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Soft-threshold at $\delta/\lambda$

nodes.name: Normalization
nodes.statement: 7)\ \mbox{\bf Normalization}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k}\GETS \sqrt{N} \frac{\mathbf{u}}{||\mathbf{u}||_2}\\
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Rescale to norm $\sqrt N$

nodes.name: Iteration
nodes.statement: 8)\ \bold{Iteration}: \mbox{Repeat from 2) until convergence.}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Repeat from step 2 until convergence

nodes.name: One-sided gradient function f'
nodes.statement: The function $f^\prime (x)$ in step 3 is defined as $f^\prime (x)=x$ for $x \le 0$ and $0$, otherwise, and it operates on a vector in a component-wise manner.

nodes.name: RFPI outer loop
nodes.statement: RFPI is a double-loop algorithm. In the outer loop the parameter $\lambda$ is increased as $\lambda_n=c \lambda_{n-1}$, where $c>1$ and $n$ are a certain constant and the counter of the outer loop, respectively. The convergent solution of $i-1$th outer loop is used for the initial state of the inner loop of the $i$th outer loop. The algorithm terminates when difference between the convergent solutions of two successive outer loops become sufficiently small.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setup
nodes.statement_short: Outer loop of RFPI: increase $\lambda$ geometrically, warm-start each inner loop, stop when successive solutions agree.

nodes.name: Increase lambda
nodes.statement: In the outer loop the parameter $\lambda$ is increased as $\lambda_n=c \lambda_{n-1}$, where $c>1$ and $n$ are a certain constant and the counter of the outer loop, respectively.

nodes.name: Partition function of the l1 recovery problem
nodes.statement: The partition function \begin{equation} Z\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right)=\int d \textrm{\boldmath $x$} \delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}\vert^{2}-N\right)e^{-\beta\vert\vert\textrm{\boldmath $x$}\vert\vert _{1}} \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left ( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0 )_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x})_\mu \right ) , \end{equation} where $\Theta\left(x \right)=1$ and $0$ for $x>0$ and $x<0$, respectively, offers the basis for our analysis.
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.statement_short: Boltzmann partition function with energy $\beta\|x\|_1$ over sign-consistent vectors on the sphere $|x|^2=N$.

nodes.name: Zero-temperature limit selects the l1 solution
nodes.statement: As $\beta$ tends to infinity, the integral of (\ref{eq:partition_func}) is dominated by the correct solution of (\ref{l1recovery}).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
conclusions: the integral of (\ref{eq:partition_func}) is dominated by the correct solution of (\ref{l1recovery})

nodes.name: Average free energy density
nodes.statement: A characteristic feature of the current problem is that (\ref{eq:partition_func}) depends on the predetermined random variables $\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi$}$ and $\textrm{\boldmath $x^{0}$} $, which requires us to assess the average of free energy density $f \equiv -(\beta N)^{-1} \left [\ln Z(\beta; \vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0}$ when evaluating the performance for typical samples of $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\vm{x}^0$.

nodes.statement: Here, $\left [\cdots \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0}$ denotes the configurational average concerning $\textrm{\boldmath $\Phi$}$ and $\textrm{\boldmath $x^{0}$}$.

nodes.name: Replica overlap order parameters
nodes.statement: Averaging (\ref{eq:expansion}) with respect to $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\vm{x}^0$ results in the saddle point evaluation concerning macroscopic variables $q_{0a} =q_{a0}\equiv N^{-1} \vm{x}^0 \cdot \vm{x}^a$ and $q_{ab}=q_{ba} \equiv N^{-1} \vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b$ ($a,b =0,1,2,\ldots,n$).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method

nodes.name: Analytic continuation of the replica number
nodes.statement: Although (\ref{eq:expansion}) holds only for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expression of $N^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n \left(\beta; \vm{\Phi}, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0} \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0}$ obtained by the saddle point evaluation under a certain assumption concerning the permutation symmetry with respect to the replica indices $a,b=1,2,\ldots n$ is obtained as an analytic function of $n$, which is likely to also hold for $n \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.statement_short: The replica expression, analytic in $n$, is assumed to extend from integer $n$ to real $n$ (replica trick).

nodes.statement_short: Under the RS ansatz and Gaussian nonzero entries, the zero-temperature average free energy is an extremum over $\chi,m,\hat Q,\hat q,\hat m$ of an explicit functional.

nodes.name: RS saddle point equations
nodes.statement: The extremization problem of (\ref{eq:free energy}) yields the following saddle point equations: \begin{eqnarray} \hat{q}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi \chi^2} \left(\arctan \left(\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m}\right) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}\right), \\ \hat{m}&=&\frac{\alpha}{\pi\chi\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2}, \\ \hat{Q}^{2}&=&2\left\{ \left(1-\rho\right)\left[\left(\hat{q}+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right) -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\hat{q}}} \right] \right . \nonumber\\ &&\left . +\rho\left[\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2+1\right)H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right) -\sqrt{\frac{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2\left(\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2\right)}}\right]\right\}, \\ \chi&=&\frac{2}{\hat{Q}}\left[\left(1-\rho\right) H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}}\right)+\rho H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right)\right], \\ m&=&\frac{2\rho\hat{m}}{\hat{Q}}H\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}}\right), \end{eqnarray} where $H(x)=\int_x^{+\infty} {\rm D}z$.

conclusions: The extremization problem of (\ref{eq:free energy}) yields the following saddle point equations:
nodes.statement_short: Stationarity of the RS free energy gives five closed equations for $\hat q,\hat m,\hat Q,\chi,m$.

nodes.name: Order parameter m is the typical overlap
nodes.statement: The value of $m$ determined by these equations physically means the typical overlap $N^{-1} \left [\vm{x}^0 \cdot \hat{\vm{x}} \right]_{\vm{\Phi}, \vm{x}^0} $ between the original signal $\vm{x}^0$ and the solution $\hat{\vm{x}}$ of (\ref{l1recovery}).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method

nodes.name: Typical direction cosine equals m over sqrt(rho)
nodes.statement: Therefore the typical value of the direction cosine between $\vm{x}^0$ and $\hat{\vm{x}}$, which serves as a performance measure of the current recovery problem, is evaluated as $\left [(\vm{x}^0 \cdot \hat{\vm{x}})/|\vm{x}^0| |\hat{\vm{x}}| \right]_{\vm{\Phi,\vm{x}^0}} =N m /(\sqrt{N \rho} \times \sqrt{N})=m/\sqrt{\rho}$.
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method

nodes.name: Mean square error (MSE)
nodes.statement: Alternatively, we may also use as a performance measure the mean square error (MSE) between the normalized vectors: \begin{eqnarray} {\rm MSE}=\left [ \left |\frac{\hat{\vm{x}}}{|\hat{\vm{x}}|}-\frac{\vm{x}^0}{|\vm{x}^0|} \right |^2 \right ]_{\vm{\Phi,\vm{x}^0}} =2\left (1-\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho}} \right ). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.statement_short: MSE between normalised recovered and true signals, equal to $2(1-m/\sqrt\rho)$.

nodes.name: AT local stability condition of the RS solution
nodes.statement: To examine the validity of the RS ansatz, we also evaluated the local stability of the RS solutions against the disturbances that break the replica symmetry \cite{AT}, which offers \begin{eqnarray} &&\frac{\alpha}{\pi (\hat{Q}\chi)^2} \arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) \cr && \times 2\left ((1-\rho)H\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}}} \right ) +\rho H\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{\hat{q}+\hat{m}^2}} \right ) \right ) -1<0, \end{eqnarray} as the stability condition.
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
nodes.statement_short: The RS solution is locally stable against replica-symmetry-breaking perturbations iff an explicit inequality in the RS order parameters holds.

nodes.name: RS solution is unstable in all examined regions
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, (\ref{AT}) is not satisfied for any regions in figures \ref{fig2} (a)--(d).
nodes.section: 3 Performance assessment by the replica method
conclusions: (\ref{AT}) is not satisfied for any regions in figures \ref{fig2} (a)--(d)

nodes.statement: This is presumably because the optimization problem for (\ref{l1recovery}) has many local optima reflecting the fact that the constraint of $||\vm{x}||_2=\sqrt{N}$ loses the convexity. This indicates that taking the replica symmetry breaking (RSB) into account is necessary for evaluating the exact performance of the signal recovery scheme defined by (\ref{l1recovery}).

nodes.statement: Excellent consistency between the curves and symbols suggests that even if (\ref{l1recovery}) has many local optima, they are close to one another in terms of the $l_2$-norm yielding similar values of MSE.

nodes.name: Sign-absorbed measurement matrix
nodes.statement: For simplicity of notations, let us first convert all the measurement results to $+1$ by multiplying $y_{\mu}$ $(\mu=1,2,\ldots, N)$ to each row of the measurement matrix $\vm{\Phi}=(\Phi_{\mu i})$ as $(\Phi_{\mu i}) \to (y_\mu \Phi_{\mu i})$, and newly denote the resultant matrix as $\vm{\Phi}=(\Phi_{\mu i})$.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm

nodes.name: Lagrangian min-max form of the recovery problem
nodes.statement: In the new notation, introduction of Lagrange multipliers $\vm{a}=(a_\mu)$ and surplus variables $\vm{z}=(z_\mu)$ converts (\ref{l1recovery}) to an unconstrained optimization problem: \begin{eqnarray} &&\mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{x},\vm{ z} > 0} \mathop{\rm max}_{\vm{a},\Lambda} \left \{ \sum_{i=1}^N |x_i|+\sum_{\mu=1}^M a_\mu \left (\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} x_i-z_\mu \right ) +\frac{\Lambda}{2}\left (\sum_{i=1}^N x_i^2-N \right ) \right \} \cr && = \mathop{\rm min}_{\vm{ x},\vm{ z} > 0} \mathop{\rm max}_{\vm{a},\Lambda} \left \{ \sum_{i=1}^N \left (\frac{\Lambda}{2} x_i^2 + |x_i| \right )-\sum_{\mu=1}^Ma_\mu z_{\mu} +\sum_{\mu,i} \Phi_{\mu i} a_\mu x_i -\frac{N\Lambda}{2} \right \}, \end{eqnarray} where $\vm{z}>0$ means that each entry of $\vm{z}$ is restricted to be positive.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.statement_short: With Lagrange multipliers $a$, surplus variables $z>0$ and $\Lambda$, the recovery problem becomes an unconstrained min-max problem.

nodes.name: Single-body cost functions
nodes.statement: In statistical mechanics, a standard approach to resolving such a difficulty is to approximate (\ref{coupled_cost}) with a bunch of optimizations for single-body cost functions parameterized as \begin{eqnarray} {\cal L}_i(x_i)=\frac{A_i}{2} x_i^2-H_i x_i +|x_i|, \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} {\cal L}_\mu(a_\mu,z_\mu) =-\frac{B_\mu}{2}a_\mu^2+K_\mu a_\mu-z_\mu a_\mu, \end{eqnarray} where $A_i,B_\mu,H_i$, and $K_\mu$ are parameters to be determined in a self-consistent manner.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the coupled cost by quadratic single-body costs for each $x_i$ and each $(a_\mu,z_\mu)$ with self-consistent parameters.

nodes.name: Cavity systems
nodes.statement: In the cavity method this is done by introducing virtual systems that are defined by removing a single variable $x_i$ or a single pair of variables $(a_\mu, z_\mu)$ from the original system \cite{cavity}.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm

nodes.name: Site-independent A and B
nodes.statement: When $N$ is sufficiently large, the law of large numbers allows us to assume that the values of $A_i$ and $B_\mu$ are constant independently of their indices; that is, that $A$ and $B$ are constants.
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm

nodes.name: Cavity self-consistent equations for 1-bit CS
nodes.statement: Under this simplification, this method yields a set of self-consistent equations: \begin{eqnarray} K_\mu &=& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i-B \hat{a}_\mu, \\ \hat{a}_\mu &=& -\frac{1}{B} f^{\prime}\left (K_\mu \right ), \\ H_i &=& \sum_{\mu =1}^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \Gamma \hat{x}_i, \\ \hat{x}_i &=& \frac{1}{A} g^{\prime}\left (H_i \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $\mu=1,2,\ldots, M$, $i=1,2,\ldots,N$, $f(u)\equiv (u^2/2)\Theta(-u)$, and $g(u)\equiv \left ((|u|-1)^2/2 \right ) \Theta \left (|u|-1 \right )$. $\Gamma$ is evaluated using $\{K_\mu\}$ and $B$ as \begin{eqnarray} \Gamma=B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime} \left (K_\mu \right ) \right ) =B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M \Theta \left (|K_\mu | -1 \right ) \right ). \end{eqnarray} $A$ is determined so that $\sum_{i=1}^N \hat{x}_i^2 =N$ holds in (\ref{BPnaive4}), which provides $B$ as \begin{eqnarray} B=A^{-1}\left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime} \left (H_i \right ) \right ) =A^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N \Theta \left (|H_i | -1\right ) \right ). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
conclusions: this method yields a set of self-consistent equations:
nodes.statement_short: The cavity method gives AMP-like fixed-point equations for $K_\mu,\hat a_\mu,H_i,\hat x_i$ with Onsager coefficient $\Gamma$ and constants $A,B$.

nodes.name: Onsager reaction term
nodes.statement: $\Gamma \hat{x}_i$ on the right-hand side of (\ref{BPnaive3}) is often referred to as the {\em Onsager reaction term} \cite{Onsager1,Onsager2}.

nodes.name: Naive cavity iterations hardly converge
nodes.statement: It is therefore unfortunate that in most cases the naive iterations of (\ref{BPnaive1})$\rightarrow$(\ref{BPnaive2}), (\ref{Gamma})$\rightarrow$(\ref{BPnaive3})$\rightarrow$(\ref{BPnaive4}), (\ref{eq:B})$\rightarrow$(\ref{BPnaive1})$\cdots$ hardly converge, which is considered a consequence of RSB \cite{Kabashima2003}, while a similar approach offers successful results for various other problems of compressed sensing \cite{Rangan2011,Bayati2011}.

nodes.name: Cavity-inspired Signal Recovery (CISR)
nodes.statement: 1)\ \mbox{\bf Initialization}:\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{X seed}: \hspace{65pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0} \GETS \hat{\mathbf{x}}^*\\ \hspace{15pt}\text{H seed}: \hspace{65pt} \mathbf{H}_0 \GETS \mathbf{H}^* \\ \hspace{15pt}\text{Counter}: \hspace{62pt} k\GETS 0\\ 2)\ \mbox{\bf Counter increase}:\\ \hspace{30pt}k \GETS k+1\\ 3)\ \mbox{\bf One-sided quadratic gradient descent}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\mathbf{H}_{k}\GETS \mathbf{H}_{k-1}-\textsc{B}^{-1}(\textsc{Y}\Phi)^{\rm T} f^\prime\left (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} \right ) \\ 4)\ \mbox{\bf Assessment of Onsager coefficient}:\\ \hspace{30pt} \Gamma \GETS (\textsc{NB})^{-1} \vm{1}^{\rm T} f^{\prime\prime} \left (\textsc{Y}\Phi \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1} \right )\\ 5)\ \mbox{\bf{Self-feedback \ cancellation}}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\tilde{\mathbf{H}}_k \GETS \mathbf{H}_{k}+\Gamma \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1}\\ 6)\ \mbox{\bf Shrinkage ($l_1$-gradient descent)}:\\ \hspace{30pt}(\mathbf{u})_i\GETS\text{sign}((\tilde{\mathbf{H}})_{i}) \text{max}\{|(\tilde{\mathbf{H}})_i|-1,0\} \ \text{for all}\ i\\ 7)\ \mbox{\bf Normalization}:\\ \hspace{30pt}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k}\GETS \sqrt{N} \frac{\mathbf{u}}{||\mathbf{u}||_2}\\ 8)\ \bold{Iteration}: \mbox{Repeat from 2) until convergence.}

nodes.name: CISR outer loop
nodes.statement: In practice, the initial value of $B$ should be set so that only a single entry becomes nonzero. This is easily done by the Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding algorithm \cite{BIHT}, which requires the number of nonzero entries as extra prior knowledge. After the initial value is set, $B$ is reduced as $B_n=r B_{n-1}$ with an appropriate constant $0<r < 1$, where $n$ is the counter of the outer loop. The algorithm terminates when the difference between the convergent solutions of two successive outer loops is sufficiently small.

However, as the length of $\vm{H}=(H_i)=\vm{\Phi}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{a}}$ is not restricted to a fixed value, the current algorithm does not need a small step size $\delta$ for the convergence.

They indicate that except in the case in which the nonzero density $\rho$ of the original signals is significantly low, CISR provides MSE values almost equal to or lower than those of RFPI.

nodes.name: Derivation of the replica moment (part A.1)
nodes.statement: Averaging (\ref{eq:expansion}) with respect to $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\vm{x}^0$ offers the following expression of the $n$-th moment of the partition function: \begin{eqnarray} &&\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}= \int \prod_{a=1}^n \left (d \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\vert^{2}-N\right) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^{0}}. \end{eqnarray} We insert $n(n+1)/2$ trivial identities \begin{eqnarray} 1=N \int dq_{ab} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $a>b=0,1,2,\ldots,n$, into (\ref{Zmoment}). Furthermore, we define a joint distribution of $n+1$ vectors $\{\vm{x}^a\}=\{\vm{x}^0, \vm{x}^1,\vm{x}^2,\ldots,\vm{x}^n \}$ as \begin{eqnarray} &&P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )= \frac{1}{V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) } P(\vm{x}^0) \times \prod_{a=1}^n \left (\delta \left (\left |\vm{x}^a\right |^2 -N \right ) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \prod_{a>b} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $\vm{Q}=(q_{ab})$ is an $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric matrix whose $00$ and the other diagonal entries are fixed as $\rho$ and $1$, respectively. $P(\vm{x}^0)=\prod_{i=1}^N \left ((1-\rho)\delta(x_i^0)+\rho \tilde{P}(x_i^0) \right )$ denotes the distribution of the original signal $\vm{x}^0$, and $V\left (\vm{Q}\right )$ is the normalization constant that makes $\int \prod_{a=0}^n d \vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )=1$ hold. These indicate that (\ref{Zmoment}) can also be expressed as \begin{eqnarray} \left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}} =\int d\vm{Q} \left (V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \times \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $d\vm{Q} \equiv \prod_{a>b}d q_{ab}$ and \begin{eqnarray} \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) =\int \prod_{a=0}^n d\vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q} \right ) \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}}. \end{eqnarray} Equation (\ref{Xi}) can be regarded as the average of $\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left((\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right)$ with respect to $\{\vm{x}^a\}$ and $\vm{\Phi}$ over distributions of $P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} \right )$ and $P(\vm{\Phi}) \equiv \left (\sqrt{2\pi/N} \right )^{-MN} \exp \left (-(N/2) \sum_{\mu,i} \Phi_{\mu i}^2 \right )$. In computing this, it is noteworthy that the central limit theorem guarantees that $u_\mu^a \equiv (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu = \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} x_i^a$ can be handled as zero-mean multivariate Gaussian random numbers whose variance and covariance are provided by \begin{eqnarray} \left [u_\mu^a u_\nu^b \right ]_{\vm{\Phi},\{\vm{x}^a\}} =\delta_{\mu \nu} q_{ab}, \end{eqnarray} when $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\{\vm{x}^a\}$ are generated independently from $P(\vm{\Phi})$ and $P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} \right )$, respectively. This means that (\ref{Xi}) can be evaluated as \begin{eqnarray} \Xi(\vm{Q}) &=&\left (\frac{\int d \vm{u} \exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^0 u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M \cr &=& \left (2 \int \frac{ d \vm{u}\exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \Theta\left (u^0 \right )\prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M. \end{eqnarray} On the other hand, expressions \begin{eqnarray} \delta\left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) =\frac{1}{4 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{aa} \exp \left (-\frac{1}{2} \hat{q}_{aa} \left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) \right ) \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} \delta\left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b -N q_{ab}\right ) =\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{ab} \exp \left ( \hat{q}_{ab} \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b-N q_{ab} \right ) \right ), \end{eqnarray} and use of the saddle point method offer \begin{eqnarray} &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q}) =\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{\vm{Q}}} \left \{ -\frac{1}{2} {\rm Tr} \hat{\vm{Q}}\vm{Q} \right . \cr && \hspace*{2cm} \left . + \ln \left ( \int d\vm{x} P(x^0) \exp \left (\frac{1}{2} \vm{x}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{Q} }\vm{x}-\beta \sum_{a=1}^n \beta |x^a| \right ) \right ) \right \}. \end{eqnarray} Here $\vm{x}=(x^0,x^1,\ldots,x^n)^{\rm T}$ and $\hat{\vm{Q}}$ is an $(n+1)\times (n+1)$ symmetric matrix whose $00$ and other diagonal components are given as $0$ and $-\hat{q}_{aa}$, respectively, while off-diagonal entries are offered as $\hat{q}_{ab}$. Equations (\ref{logXi}) and (\ref{logV}) indicate that $N^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n (\beta;\vm{\Phi}, \vm{x}^0 ) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}, \vm{x}^0}$ is correctly evaluated by using the saddle point method with respect to $\vm{Q}$ in the assessment of the right-hand side of (\ref{Zn}) when $N$ and $M$ tend to infinity keeping $\alpha=M/N$ finite.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.statement_short: Replica computation: average $Z^n$ over $\Phi$ and $x^0$ by introducing overlap order parameters and applying the central limit theorem and saddle-point method.

nodes.name: Derivation of the RS free energy (part A.2)
nodes.statement: Let us assume that the relevant saddle point in assessing (\ref{Zn}) is of the form of (\ref{RSanzats}) and, accordingly, \begin{eqnarray} \hat{q}_{ab}=\hat{q}_{ba} =\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} 0, &( \mbox{$a=b=0$})\\ \hat{m}, &( \mbox{$a=1,2,\ldots,n$; $b=0$})\\ \hat{Q}, &( \mbox{$a=b=1,2,\ldots,n$})\\ \hat{q}, &( \mbox{$a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n$}) \end{array} \right . . \end{eqnarray} $n+1$ dimensional Gaussian random variables $u^0,u^1,\ldots u^n$ whose variance and covariance are provided as (\ref{RSanzats}) can be expressed as \begin{eqnarray} && u^0=\sqrt{\rho-\frac{m^2}{q}}s^0 + \frac{m}{\sqrt{q}} z, \\ && u^a=\sqrt{1-q} s^a+ \sqrt{q} z, \ (a=1,2,\ldots,n) \end{eqnarray} utilizing $n+2$ independent standard Gaussian random variables $z$ and $s^0,s^1,\ldots,s^n$. This indicates that (\ref{logXi}) is evaluated as \begin{eqnarray} \Xi(\vm{Q})=\left ( 2 \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) H^n \left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \right )^M. \end{eqnarray} On the other hand, substituting (\ref{RShatQ}) into (\ref{logV}), in conjunction with the identity \begin{eqnarray} \exp \left (\hat{q} \sum_{a>b(\ge 1)} x^a x^b \right )=\int {\rm D}z \exp \left (\sum_{a=1}^n \left ( -\frac{\hat{q}}{2} (x^a)^2 + \sqrt{\hat{q}} z x^a \right ) \right ) \end{eqnarray} provides \begin{eqnarray} &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q} )=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{Q}, \hat{q},\hat{m} } \left \{ \frac{n}{2}\hat{Q}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \hat{q}q -\hat{m} m \right . \cr &&\left . +\ln \left [\left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q} \!+\! \hat{q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\!\beta |x| \right ) \right )^n \right ]_{x^0,z} \right \}. \end{eqnarray} Although we have assumed that $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expressions of (\ref{NewXi}) and (\ref{NewV}) are likely to hold for $n \in \mathbb{R}$ as well. Therefore the average free energy $\overline{f}$ can be evaluated by substituting these expressions into the formula $\overline{f}= -\lim_{n\to 0} (\partial/\partial n) \left ((\beta N)^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n (\beta; \vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0 ) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0} \right )$. In the limit of $\beta \to \infty$, a nontrivial saddle point is obtained only when $\chi \equiv \beta (1-q)$ is kept finite. Accordingly, we change the notations of the auxiliary variables as $\hat{Q}+\hat{q} \to \beta \hat{Q}$, $\hat{q} \to \beta^2 \hat{q}$, and $\hat{m} \to \beta \hat{m}$. Furthermore, we use the asymptotic forms \begin{eqnarray} &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) \ln H\left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \cr &&=\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho -m^2} }z \right )\left (-\frac{z^2}{2\chi} \Theta(z) \right ) \cr &&= -\frac{1}{4 \pi \chi}\left (\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2} \right ) \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta} \ln \left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left (\beta \left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\! |x| \right ) \right ) \right ) \cr && =-\phi\left (\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0;\hat{Q} \right ). \end{eqnarray} Using these in the resultant expression of $\overline{f}$ offers (\ref{eq:free energy}).
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.statement_short: Impose the RS ansatz, decouple replicas with Gaussian variables, continue $n\to0$ and take $\beta\to\infty$ with $\chi=\beta(1-q)$ fixed to obtain (7).

nodes.name: Derivation of the RS stability condition
nodes.statement: The 1-step replica symmetry breaking (1RSB) ansatz means that, at the relevant saddle point, $n$ replica indices $1,2,\ldots,n$ are classified into $n/p$ groups of an equal size $p$, and $q_{ab}=q_1$ holds if $a$ and $b$ belong to an identical group and $q_0(\le q_1)$, otherwise. This yields the following expression of the average free energy of finite temperature: \begin{eqnarray} &&\overline{f}=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\omega}\left \{ -\frac{1}{\beta } \left [ \ln \left (\int {\rm D}{t} \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_0 \right ) \right ) \right ]_{x^0,z} \right . \cr && \hspace*{0cm}-\frac{1}{2\beta}(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)+\frac{\hat{q}_1}{2\beta} (1-q_1)+\frac{p}{2\beta} (\hat{q}_1q_1-\hat{q}_0q_0 )+\frac{1}{\beta}\hat{m}m\cr && \hspace*{0cm}\left . -\frac{2\alpha}{\beta p}\! \int \! {\rm D}z H\left (\!\frac{m }{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z\! \right ) \ln \left (\int {\rm D}t \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_1 \right ) \right ) \right \}, \end{eqnarray} where ${\cal Y}_0\equiv -\ln \left (\int dx \exp \left (-(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)x^2 /2 + (\sqrt{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0}t+\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z +\hat{m}x^0 )x-\beta |x| \right ) \right )$, ${\cal Y}_1\equiv - \ln \left (\int {\rm D}x \Theta\left (-\left (\sqrt{1-q_1}x+\sqrt{q_1-q_0}t+\sqrt{q}_0 z \right ) \right ) \right )$, $\omega=\{q_1,q_0,m,\hat{Q},\hat{q}_1, \hat{q}_0, \hat{m} \}$, and $\left [\cdots \right]_{x^0,z}=\int dx^0 P(x^0)\int {\rm D}z \left (\cdots \right )$. The RS solution is regarded as a special case of the 1RSB solution for which $q_1=q_0 $ holds. Therefore one can check the thermodynamical validity of the RS solution by examining the stability of the solution of $q_1=q_0$ under the 1RSB ansatz. The extremization condition of (\ref{1RSB}) indicates that \begin{eqnarray} &&q_1-q_0=\left [ \frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )^2} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right . \cr &&\hspace*{4cm} \left . - \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t^2}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} -\left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right )\right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0) \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0) \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} &&\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0=2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left ( \frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p{\cal Y}_1} \left ( \partial{\cal Y}_1/\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) \right )^2} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right . \cr &&\hspace*{4cm} \left . - \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_1/\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) \right )} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right )^2 \right ) \cr &&\phantom{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0} \simeq 2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2\cr && \hspace*{4cm} \times \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} t^2}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} -\left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} t}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right )^2 \right ) (q_1-q_0)\cr &&\phantom{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0} \simeq 2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 (q_1-q_0) \end{eqnarray} hold for $|q_1-q_0| \ll 1$ and $|\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0| \ll 1$ irrespectively of the value of $p$. Here ${\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}$ and ${\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS}$ represent assessments of ${\cal Y}_0$ and ${\cal Y}_1$ under the assumptions of $\hat{q}_1=\hat{q}_0$ and $q_1=q_0$, respectively. In (\ref{AT1}) and (\ref{AT2}) we used the Taylor expansion expressions $\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \sim \partial{\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS} /\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) + \partial^2{\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS} /\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z)^2 \sqrt{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0} t$ and $\partial{\cal Y}_1/\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) \sim \partial{\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS} /\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) + \partial^2{\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS} /\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z)^2 \sqrt{q_1-q_0} t$, and the fact that the variances of $t$ for the measures ${\rm D}te^{-p {\cal Y}_0}/\int {\rm D}te^{-p {\cal Y}_0}$ and ${\rm D}te^{-p {\cal Y}_1}/\int {\rm D}te^{-p {\cal Y}_1}$ become unity as $\hat{q}_1 - \hat{q}_0$ and $q_1 -q_0$ vanish, irrespectively of the value of $p$. To examine the stability of the RS solution in the limit of $\beta \to \infty$, let us change the variable notations as $\chi=\beta(1-q)$, $\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1 \to \beta \hat{Q}$, $\hat{q}_1\to \beta^2 \hat{q}_1$, $\hat{q}_0 \to \beta^2 \hat{q}_0$, and $\hat{m}\to \beta \hat{m}$ and set $q_0=q$ and $\hat{q}_0=\hat{q}$. This yields expressions of ${\cal Y}^{\rm RS}_0 \simeq \beta \phi(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0; \hat{Q}) = -\beta g(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0)/\hat{Q}$ and ${\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS} \simeq (\beta/\chi) f(-\sqrt{q}z )$ for $\beta \gg 1$. Substituting these into (\ref{AT1}) and (\ref{AT2}) leads to \begin{eqnarray} \Delta \simeq \frac{1}{\hat{Q}^2} \left [ \left ( g^{\rm \prime \prime}(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0) \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} \hat{\Delta} \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} \hat{\Delta} \simeq \frac{2\alpha}{\chi^2} \int {\rm D}z H \left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}} z\right ) \left ( f^{\prime \prime} (-z) \right )^2 \Delta, \end{eqnarray} where we set $\Delta=q_1-q$ and $\hat{\Delta}=\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}$, and used $q\to 1$. The condition that (\ref{AT1new}) and (\ref{AT2new}) allow a solution of $(\Delta,\hat{\Delta}) \ne (0,0)$ offers (\ref{AT}).
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.statement_short: Embed RS in the 1RSB ansatz and linearise the 1RSB saddle-point equations around $q_1=q_0$; a nonzero solution of the linear system gives the AT condition.

nodes.name: Derivation of the cavity equations
nodes.section: C Derivation of the cavity equations
nodes.statement_short: Cavity argument: vertical and horizontal message steps for cavity cost parameters, then large-$N$ expansion of the messages yields the Onsager-corrected equations (19)-(22).

nodes.name: Average the replicated partition function
nodes.statement: Averaging (\ref{eq:expansion}) with respect to $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\vm{x}^0$ offers the following expression of the $n$-th moment of the partition function: \begin{eqnarray} &&\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}= \int \prod_{a=1}^n \left (d \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\vert^{2}-N\right) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^{0}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Average the $n$-th moment over $\Phi$ and $x^0$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Insert overlap identities
nodes.statement: We insert $n(n+1)/2$ trivial identities \begin{eqnarray} 1=N \int dq_{ab} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $a>b=0,1,2,\ldots,n$, into (\ref{Zmoment}).
nodes.statement_short: Insert delta-function identities defining the overlaps $q_{ab}$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Define the replica joint distribution
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we define a joint distribution of $n+1$ vectors $\{\vm{x}^a\}=\{\vm{x}^0, \vm{x}^1,\vm{x}^2,\ldots,\vm{x}^n \}$ as \begin{eqnarray} &&P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )= \frac{1}{V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) } P(\vm{x}^0) \times \prod_{a=1}^n \left (\delta \left (\left |\vm{x}^a\right |^2 -N \right ) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \prod_{a>b} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $\vm{Q}=(q_{ab})$ is an $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric matrix whose $00$ and the other diagonal entries are fixed as $\rho$ and $1$, respectively. $P(\vm{x}^0)=\prod_{i=1}^N \left ((1-\rho)\delta(x_i^0)+\rho \tilde{P}(x_i^0) \right )$ denotes the distribution of the original signal $\vm{x}^0$, and $V\left (\vm{Q}\right )$ is the normalization constant that makes $\int \prod_{a=0}^n d \vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )=1$ hold.
nodes.statement_short: Define the joint distribution of replicas given $Q$ and its normaliser $V(Q)$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Rewrite the moment as an integral over Q
nodes.statement: These indicate that (\ref{Zmoment}) can also be expressed as \begin{eqnarray} \left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}} =\int d\vm{Q} \left (V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \times \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \right ), \end{eqnarray} where $d\vm{Q} \equiv \prod_{a>b}d q_{ab}$ and \begin{eqnarray} \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) =\int \prod_{a=0}^n d\vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q} \right ) \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Express the moment as an integral of $V(Q)\Xi(Q)$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Evaluate Xi by the central limit theorem
nodes.statement: Equation (\ref{Xi}) can be regarded as the average of $\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left((\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right)$ with respect to $\{\vm{x}^a\}$ and $\vm{\Phi}$ over distributions of $P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} \right )$ and $P(\vm{\Phi}) \equiv \left (\sqrt{2\pi/N} \right )^{-MN} \exp \left (-(N/2) \sum_{\mu,i} \Phi_{\mu i}^2 \right )$. In computing this, it is noteworthy that the central limit theorem guarantees that $u_\mu^a \equiv (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu = \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} x_i^a$ can be handled as zero-mean multivariate Gaussian random numbers whose variance and covariance are provided by \begin{eqnarray} \left [u_\mu^a u_\nu^b \right ]_{\vm{\Phi},\{\vm{x}^a\}} =\delta_{\mu \nu} q_{ab}, \end{eqnarray} when $\vm{\Phi}$ and $\{\vm{x}^a\}$ are generated independently from $P(\vm{\Phi})$ and $P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} \right )$, respectively. This means that (\ref{Xi}) can be evaluated as \begin{eqnarray} \Xi(\vm{Q}) &=&\left (\frac{\int d \vm{u} \exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^0 u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M \cr &=& \left (2 \int \frac{ d \vm{u}\exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \Theta\left (u^0 \right )\prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Treat $u^a_\mu$ as correlated Gaussians (central limit theorem) to evaluate $\Xi(Q)$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Evaluate V by Fourier representation and saddle point
nodes.statement: On the other hand, expressions \begin{eqnarray} \delta\left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) =\frac{1}{4 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{aa} \exp \left (-\frac{1}{2} \hat{q}_{aa} \left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) \right ) \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} \delta\left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b -N q_{ab}\right ) =\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{ab} \exp \left ( \hat{q}_{ab} \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b-N q_{ab} \right ) \right ), \end{eqnarray} and use of the saddle point method offer \begin{eqnarray} &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q}) =\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{\vm{Q}}} \left \{ -\frac{1}{2} {\rm Tr} \hat{\vm{Q}}\vm{Q} \right . \cr && \hspace*{2cm} \left . + \ln \left ( \int d\vm{x} P(x^0) \exp \left (\frac{1}{2} \vm{x}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{Q} }\vm{x}-\beta \sum_{a=1}^n \beta |x^a| \right ) \right ) \right \}. \end{eqnarray} Here $\vm{x}=(x^0,x^1,\ldots,x^n)^{\rm T}$ and $\hat{\vm{Q}}$ is an $(n+1)\times (n+1)$ symmetric matrix whose $00$ and other diagonal components are given as $0$ and $-\hat{q}_{aa}$, respectively, while off-diagonal entries are offered as $\hat{q}_{ab}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier-represent the delta functions and evaluate $\ln V(Q)$ by the saddle-point method
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Saddle point over Q is exact
nodes.statement: Equations (\ref{logXi}) and (\ref{logV}) indicate that $N^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n (\beta;\vm{\Phi}, \vm{x}^0 ) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}, \vm{x}^0}$ is correctly evaluated by using the saddle point method with respect to $\vm{Q}$ in the assessment of the right-hand side of (\ref{Zn}) when $N$ and $M$ tend to infinity keeping $\alpha=M/N$ finite.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude that the saddle point over $Q$ evaluates the moment for large $N,M$
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Impose the RS ansatz
nodes.statement: Let us assume that the relevant saddle point in assessing (\ref{Zn}) is of the form of (\ref{RSanzats}) and, accordingly, \begin{eqnarray} \hat{q}_{ab}=\hat{q}_{ba} =\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} 0, &( \mbox{$a=b=0$})\\ \hat{m}, &( \mbox{$a=1,2,\ldots,n$; $b=0$})\\ \hat{Q}, &( \mbox{$a=b=1,2,\ldots,n$})\\ \hat{q}, &( \mbox{$a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n$}) \end{array} \right . . \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Assume replica-symmetric $Q$ and $\hat Q$
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Gaussian decoupling of Xi
nodes.statement: $n+1$ dimensional Gaussian random variables $u^0,u^1,\ldots u^n$ whose variance and covariance are provided as (\ref{RSanzats}) can be expressed as \begin{eqnarray} && u^0=\sqrt{\rho-\frac{m^2}{q}}s^0 + \frac{m}{\sqrt{q}} z, \\ && u^a=\sqrt{1-q} s^a+ \sqrt{q} z, \ (a=1,2,\ldots,n) \end{eqnarray} utilizing $n+2$ independent standard Gaussian random variables $z$ and $s^0,s^1,\ldots,s^n$. This indicates that (\ref{logXi}) is evaluated as \begin{eqnarray} \Xi(\vm{Q})=\left ( 2 \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) H^n \left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \right )^M. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Represent correlated Gaussians via independent ones to get $\Xi(Q)$ under RS
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: RS expression for V
nodes.statement: On the other hand, substituting (\ref{RShatQ}) into (\ref{logV}), in conjunction with the identity \begin{eqnarray} \exp \left (\hat{q} \sum_{a>b(\ge 1)} x^a x^b \right )=\int {\rm D}z \exp \left (\sum_{a=1}^n \left ( -\frac{\hat{q}}{2} (x^a)^2 + \sqrt{\hat{q}} z x^a \right ) \right ) \end{eqnarray} provides \begin{eqnarray} &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q} )=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{Q}, \hat{q},\hat{m} } \left \{ \frac{n}{2}\hat{Q}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \hat{q}q -\hat{m} m \right . \cr &&\left . +\ln \left [\left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q} \!+\! \hat{q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\!\beta |x| \right ) \right )^n \right ]_{x^0,z} \right \}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Hubbard-Stratonovich identity gives $\ln V(Q)$ under RS
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Replica limit
nodes.statement: Although we have assumed that $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expressions of (\ref{NewXi}) and (\ref{NewV}) are likely to hold for $n \in \mathbb{R}$ as well. Therefore the average free energy $\overline{f}$ can be evaluated by substituting these expressions into the formula $\overline{f}= -\lim_{n\to 0} (\partial/\partial n) \left ((\beta N)^{-1} \ln \left [Z^n (\beta; \vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0 ) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^0} \right )$.
nodes.statement_short: Continue to real $n$ and take $n\to0$ for the free energy
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Zero-temperature scaling
nodes.statement: In the limit of $\beta \to \infty$, a nontrivial saddle point is obtained only when $\chi \equiv \beta (1-q)$ is kept finite. Accordingly, we change the notations of the auxiliary variables as $\hat{Q}+\hat{q} \to \beta \hat{Q}$, $\hat{q} \to \beta^2 \hat{q}$, and $\hat{m} \to \beta \hat{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale the order parameters for $\beta\to\infty$ with $\chi$ finite
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Asymptotic forms
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we use the asymptotic forms \begin{eqnarray} &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) \ln H\left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \cr &&=\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho -m^2} }z \right )\left (-\frac{z^2}{2\chi} \Theta(z) \right ) \cr &&= -\frac{1}{4 \pi \chi}\left (\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2} \right ) \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta} \ln \left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left (\beta \left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\! |x| \right ) \right ) \right ) \cr && =-\phi\left (\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0;\hat{Q} \right ). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the two $\beta\to\infty$ asymptotic integrals
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Conclude the RS free energy
nodes.statement: Using these in the resultant expression of $\overline{f}$ offers (\ref{eq:free energy}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine to obtain (7)
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: 1RSB free energy
nodes.statement: The 1-step replica symmetry breaking (1RSB) ansatz means that, at the relevant saddle point, $n$ replica indices $1,2,\ldots,n$ are classified into $n/p$ groups of an equal size $p$, and $q_{ab}=q_1$ holds if $a$ and $b$ belong to an identical group and $q_0(\le q_1)$, otherwise. This yields the following expression of the average free energy of finite temperature: \begin{eqnarray} &&\overline{f}=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\omega}\left \{ -\frac{1}{\beta } \left [ \ln \left (\int {\rm D}{t} \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_0 \right ) \right ) \right ]_{x^0,z} \right . \cr && \hspace*{0cm}-\frac{1}{2\beta}(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)+\frac{\hat{q}_1}{2\beta} (1-q_1)+\frac{p}{2\beta} (\hat{q}_1q_1-\hat{q}_0q_0 )+\frac{1}{\beta}\hat{m}m\cr && \hspace*{0cm}\left . -\frac{2\alpha}{\beta p}\! \int \! {\rm D}z H\left (\!\frac{m }{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z\! \right ) \ln \left (\int {\rm D}t \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_1 \right ) \right ) \right \}, \end{eqnarray} where ${\cal Y}_0\equiv -\ln \left (\int dx \exp \left (-(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)x^2 /2 + (\sqrt{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0}t+\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z +\hat{m}x^0 )x-\beta |x| \right ) \right )$, ${\cal Y}_1\equiv - \ln \left (\int {\rm D}x \Theta\left (-\left (\sqrt{1-q_1}x+\sqrt{q_1-q_0}t+\sqrt{q}_0 z \right ) \right ) \right )$, $\omega=\{q_1,q_0,m,\hat{Q},\hat{q}_1, \hat{q}_0, \hat{m} \}$, and $\left [\cdots \right]_{x^0,z}=\int dx^0 P(x^0)\int {\rm D}z \left (\cdots \right )$. The RS solution is regarded as a special case of the 1RSB solution for which $q_1=q_0 $ holds.
nodes.statement_short: Define the 1RSB ansatz, its free energy (44), and note RS is the case $q_1=q_0$
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution

nodes.name: Reduce to stability under 1RSB
nodes.statement: Therefore one can check the thermodynamical validity of the RS solution by examining the stability of the solution of $q_1=q_0$ under the 1RSB ansatz.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce RS validity to stability of $q_1=q_0$ under 1RSB
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution

nodes.name: Recovery step
nodes.statement: \noindent{\bf Recovery step:}\\ $A_i$ and $H_i$ are evaluated from (\ref{HstepB}) and (\ref{HstepK}) as \begin{eqnarray} A_i&=&\Lambda+\sum_{\mu=1}^M \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}^2}{B_{\mu \to i}} f^{\prime \prime} (K_{\mu \to i}), \\ H_i&=& - \sum_{\mu=1}^M \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}}{B_{\mu \to i} } f^{\prime }(K_{\mu \to i}). \end{eqnarray} This means that the recovered signal is provided as \begin{eqnarray} \hat{x}_i =\frac{1}{A_i} g^\prime(H_i), \end{eqnarray} where $\Lambda$ is determined in such a way that $\sum_{i=1}^N \hat{x}_i^2 =N$ holds. Similarly, \begin{eqnarray} B_\mu&=& \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}^2}{A_{i \to \mu}} g^{\prime \prime}(H_{i \to \mu}), \\ K_\mu&=& \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}}{A_{i \to \mu}}g^{\prime}(H_{i \to \mu}), \end{eqnarray} are obtained from (\ref{VstepA}) and (\ref{VstepH}). These offer the (approximate) optimal value of the Lagrange multiplier $a_\mu$ as \begin{eqnarray} \hat{a}_\mu=-\frac{1}{B_\mu} f^\prime(K_\mu). \end{eqnarray} Equations (\ref{VstepH}) and (\ref{RstepH}) indicate the difference between $H_{i \to \mu }$ and $H_{i}$ is vanishingly small for $N \to \infty$ as $\Phi_{\mu i}$ scales as $O\left (N^{-1/2} \right )$, and similarly for $K_{\mu \to i}$ and $K_\mu$. This also allows us to handle $A_i$ and $A_{i \to \mu}$ as a single site-independent parameter $A$, and we similarly deal with $B_\mu $ and $B_{\mu \to i}$ as $B$. These considerations, in conjunction with (\ref{RstepA}) and (\ref{RstepB}), offer \begin{eqnarray} A&=&\Lambda+\frac{1}{NB} \sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu ), \\ B&=& \frac{1}{NA}\sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime}(H_i), \end{eqnarray} where we replaced $\Phi_{\mu i}^2$ in (\ref{RstepA}) and (\ref{RstepB}) with its expectation $N^{-1}$ by utilizing the law of large numbers. Furthermore, inserting $f^{\prime}(K_{\mu \to i}) \simeq f^{\prime}(K_\mu-\Phi_{\mu i}\hat{x}_i) \simeq f^{\prime}(K_\mu)-\Phi_{\mu i} f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \hat{x}_i$ and $g^{\prime}(H_{i \to \mu}) \simeq g^{\prime}(H_i+ \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu ) \simeq g^{\prime}(H_i)+\Phi_{\mu i} g^{\prime \prime}(H_i) \hat{a}_\mu$ into (\ref{RstepH}) and (\ref{RstepK}), respectively, yields \begin{eqnarray} H_i &\simeq&\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{B}\sum_{\mu=1}^M \Phi_{\mu i}^2 f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i \cr &\simeq &\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{NB}\sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i \cr &=& \sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \Gamma \hat{x}_i \end{eqnarray} and \begin{eqnarray} K_\mu &\simeq& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{A}\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i}^2 g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr &\simeq & \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{N A}\sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr &=& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -B \hat{a}_\mu , \end{eqnarray} where we set $\Gamma=(NB)^{-1}\sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu)$. Equations (\ref{recoveredX}), (\ref{recovereda}), and (\ref{singleA})--(\ref{singleK}) lead to (\ref{BPnaive1})--(\ref{BPnaive4}).

nodes.name: Onsager coefficient Gamma
nodes.statement: \Gamma=B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime} \left (K_\mu \right ) \right ) =B^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{\mu=1}^M \Theta \left (|K_\mu | -1 \right ) \right ).
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: Gamma

nodes.name: Equation for B
nodes.statement: B=A^{-1}\left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime} \left (H_i \right ) \right ) =A^{-1} \left (N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N \Theta \left (|H_i | -1\right ) \right ).
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: eq:B

nodes.name: Modified update of a_mu
nodes.statement: \hat{a}_\mu &=& \hat{a}_\mu -\frac{1}{B} f^{\prime}\left (\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i \right ),
nodes.section: 4 Cavity-inspired signal recovery algorithm
nodes.label: BPnaive2rev

nodes.name: Averaged n-th moment
nodes.statement: &&\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}= \int \prod_{a=1}^n \left (d \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\delta\left(\vert \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^a\vert^{2}-N\right) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi},\vm{x}^{0}}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Zmoment

nodes.name: Overlap identity
nodes.statement: 1=N \int dq_{ab} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Replica joint distribution
nodes.statement: &&P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q}\right )= \frac{1}{V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) } P(\vm{x}^0) \times \prod_{a=1}^n \left (\delta \left (\left |\vm{x}^a\right |^2 -N \right ) \times e^{-\beta||\textrm{\boldmath $x^a$}||_{1}} \right ) \cr && \hspace*{3cm} \times \prod_{a>b} \delta \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b - N q_{ab} \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: replica_joint_dist

nodes.name: Moment as integral over Q
nodes.statement: \left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}} =\int d\vm{Q} \left (V\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \times \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Zn

nodes.name: Definition of Xi(Q)
nodes.statement: \Xi\left (\vm{Q}\right ) =\int \prod_{a=0}^n d\vm{x}^a P\left (\{\vm{x}^a\} |\vm{Q} \right ) \left[\prod_{a=1}^n \prod_{\mu=1}^M \Theta\left( (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^0)_\mu (\vm{\Phi} \vm{x}^a)_\mu \right) \right]_{\vm{\Phi}}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: Xi

nodes.name: Covariance of u
nodes.statement: \left [u_\mu^a u_\nu^b \right ]_{\vm{\Phi},\{\vm{x}^a\}} =\delta_{\mu \nu} q_{ab},
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Gaussian evaluation of Xi(Q)
nodes.statement: \Xi(\vm{Q}) &=&\left (\frac{\int d \vm{u} \exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^0 u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M \cr &=& \left (2 \int \frac{ d \vm{u}\exp\left (-\frac{1}{2}\vm{u}^{\rm T} \vm{Q}^{-1} \vm{u} \right ) \Theta\left (u^0 \right )\prod_{a=1}^n \Theta\left (u^a \right ) }{ (2\pi)^{(n+1)/2} (\det \vm{Q})^{1/2}} \right )^M.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: logXi

nodes.name: Fourier representation of norm delta
nodes.statement: \delta\left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) =\frac{1}{4 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{aa} \exp \left (-\frac{1}{2} \hat{q}_{aa} \left (|\vm{x}^a|^2-N \right ) \right )
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Fourier representation of overlap delta
nodes.statement: \delta\left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b -N q_{ab}\right ) =\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{-{\rm i}\infty}^{+{\rm i}\infty} d \hat{q}_{ab} \exp \left ( \hat{q}_{ab} \left (\vm{x}^a \cdot \vm{x}^b-N q_{ab} \right ) \right ),
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Saddle point expression for ln V(Q)
nodes.statement: &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q}) =\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{\vm{Q}}} \left \{ -\frac{1}{2} {\rm Tr} \hat{\vm{Q}}\vm{Q} \right . \cr && \hspace*{2cm} \left . + \ln \left ( \int d\vm{x} P(x^0) \exp \left (\frac{1}{2} \vm{x}^{\rm T} \hat{\vm{Q} }\vm{x}-\beta \sum_{a=1}^n \beta |x^a| \right ) \right ) \right \}.
nodes.section: A.1 Assessment of $\left[Z^{n}\left(\beta; \Phi, \textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}\right)\right]_{\Phi,\textrm{\boldmath $x$}^{0}}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$
nodes.label: logV

nodes.name: RS ansatz for conjugate parameters
nodes.statement: \hat{q}_{ab}=\hat{q}_{ba} =\left \{ \begin{array}{ll} 0, &( \mbox{$a=b=0$})\\ \hat{m}, &( \mbox{$a=1,2,\ldots,n$; $b=0$})\\ \hat{Q}, &( \mbox{$a=b=1,2,\ldots,n$})\\ \hat{q}, &( \mbox{$a\ne b =1,2,\ldots,n$}) \end{array} \right . .
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: RShatQ

nodes.name: Gaussian representation of u under RS
nodes.statement: && u^0=\sqrt{\rho-\frac{m^2}{q}}s^0 + \frac{m}{\sqrt{q}} z, \\ && u^a=\sqrt{1-q} s^a+ \sqrt{q} z, \ (a=1,2,\ldots,n)
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: Newgauss0

nodes.name: RS expression of Xi(Q)
nodes.statement: \Xi(\vm{Q})=\left ( 2 \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) H^n \left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \right )^M.
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: NewXi

nodes.name: Hubbard-Stratonovich identity
nodes.statement: \exp \left (\hat{q} \sum_{a>b(\ge 1)} x^a x^b \right )=\int {\rm D}z \exp \left (\sum_{a=1}^n \left ( -\frac{\hat{q}}{2} (x^a)^2 + \sqrt{\hat{q}} z x^a \right ) \right )
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: RS expression of ln V(Q)
nodes.statement: &&\frac{1}{N} \ln V(\vm{Q} )=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\hat{Q}, \hat{q},\hat{m} } \left \{ \frac{n}{2}\hat{Q}-\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \hat{q}q -\hat{m} m \right . \cr &&\left . +\ln \left [\left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q} \!+\! \hat{q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\!\beta |x| \right ) \right )^n \right ]_{x^0,z} \right \}.
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz
nodes.label: NewV

nodes.name: Zero-temperature asymptotic of Xi term
nodes.statement: &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta}\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2} }z \right ) \ln H\left (\sqrt{\frac{q}{1-q}} z \right ) \cr &&=\int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho -m^2} }z \right )\left (-\frac{z^2}{2\chi} \Theta(z) \right ) \cr &&= -\frac{1}{4 \pi \chi}\left (\arctan \left (\frac{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}}{m} \right ) -\frac{m}{\rho}\sqrt{\rho-m^2} \right )
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: Zero-temperature asymptotic of V term
nodes.statement: &&\lim_{\beta \to \infty}\frac{1}{\beta} \ln \left ( \! \int \! dx \exp \!\left (\beta \left ( \! -\frac{\hat{Q}}{2} x^2\!+\!\left (\!\sqrt{\hat{q}}z \!+\! \hat{m} x^0 \!\right ) \!x \!-\! |x| \right ) \right ) \right ) \cr && =-\phi\left (\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0;\hat{Q} \right ).
nodes.section: A.2 Treatment under the replica symmetric ansatz

nodes.name: 1RSB free energy
nodes.statement: &&\overline{f}=\mathop{\rm extr}_{\omega}\left \{ -\frac{1}{\beta } \left [ \ln \left (\int {\rm D}{t} \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_0 \right ) \right ) \right ]_{x^0,z} \right . \cr && \hspace*{0cm}-\frac{1}{2\beta}(\hat{Q}+\hat{q}_1)+\frac{\hat{q}_1}{2\beta} (1-q_1)+\frac{p}{2\beta} (\hat{q}_1q_1-\hat{q}_0q_0 )+\frac{1}{\beta}\hat{m}m\cr && \hspace*{0cm}\left . -\frac{2\alpha}{\beta p}\! \int \! {\rm D}z H\left (\!\frac{m }{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z\! \right ) \ln \left (\int {\rm D}t \exp \left (-p {\cal Y}_1 \right ) \right ) \right \},
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: 1RSB

nodes.name: Linearised 1RSB condition for q
nodes.statement: &&q_1-q_0=\left [ \frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )^2} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right . \cr &&\hspace*{4cm} \left . - \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_0/\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0} z) \right )} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t^2}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} -\left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0} t}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_0}} \right )^2 \right )\right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0) \cr &&\phantom{q_1-q_0} \simeq \left [ \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_0^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{\hat{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} (\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0)
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: AT1

nodes.name: Linearised 1RSB condition for q-hat
nodes.statement: &&\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0=2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left ( \frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p{\cal Y}_1} \left ( \partial{\cal Y}_1/\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) \right )^2} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right . \cr &&\hspace*{4cm} \left . - \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} \left (\partial{\cal Y}_1/\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0} z) \right )} {\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right )^2 \right ) \cr &&\phantom{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0} \simeq 2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2\cr && \hspace*{4cm} \times \left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} t^2}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} -\left (\frac{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1} t}{\int {\rm D}t e^{-p {\cal Y}_1}} \right )^2 \right ) (q_1-q_0)\cr &&\phantom{\hat{q}_1-\hat{q}_0} \simeq 2 \alpha \int {\rm D}z H\left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho q-m^2}}z \right ) \left (\frac{\partial^2 {\cal Y}_1^{\rm RS}}{\partial (\sqrt{{q}_0}z )^2} \right )^2 (q_1-q_0)
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: AT2

nodes.name: Linear relation for Delta
nodes.statement: \Delta \simeq \frac{1}{\hat{Q}^2} \left [ \left ( g^{\rm \prime \prime}(\sqrt{\hat{q}}z+\hat{m}x^0) \right )^2 \right ]_{x^0,z} \hat{\Delta}
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: AT1new

nodes.name: Linear relation for Delta-hat
nodes.statement: \hat{\Delta} \simeq \frac{2\alpha}{\chi^2} \int {\rm D}z H \left (\frac{m}{\sqrt{\rho-m^2}} z\right ) \left ( f^{\prime \prime} (-z) \right )^2 \Delta,
nodes.section: B Stability of the RS solution
nodes.label: AT2new

nodes.statement: A_i&=&\Lambda+\sum_{\mu=1}^M \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}^2}{B_{\mu \to i}} f^{\prime \prime} (K_{\mu \to i}),

nodes.statement: H_i&=& - \sum_{\mu=1}^M \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}}{B_{\mu \to i} } f^{\prime }(K_{\mu \to i}).

nodes.statement: \hat{x}_i =\frac{1}{A_i} g^\prime(H_i),

nodes.statement: B_\mu&=& \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}^2}{A_{i \to \mu}} g^{\prime \prime}(H_{i \to \mu}),

nodes.statement: K_\mu&=& \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\Phi_{\mu i}}{A_{i \to \mu}}g^{\prime}(H_{i \to \mu}),

nodes.statement: \hat{a}_\mu=-\frac{1}{B_\mu} f^\prime(K_\mu).

nodes.statement: A&=&\Lambda+\frac{1}{NB} \sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu ),

nodes.statement: B&=& \frac{1}{NA}\sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime}(H_i),

nodes.name: Expanded H_i with Onsager term
nodes.statement: H_i &\simeq&\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{B}\sum_{\mu=1}^M \Phi_{\mu i}^2 f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i \cr &\simeq &\sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \left (\frac{1}{NB}\sum_{\mu=1}^M f^{\prime \prime}(K_\mu) \right ) \hat{x}_i \cr &=& \sum_{\mu=1 }^M \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{a}_\mu + \Gamma \hat{x}_i

nodes.name: Expanded K_mu
nodes.statement: K_\mu &\simeq& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{A}\sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i}^2 g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr &\simeq & \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -\left (\frac{1}{N A}\sum_{i=1}^N g^{\prime \prime} (H_i) \right )\hat{a}_\mu \cr &=& \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_{\mu i} \hat{x}_i -B \hat{a}_\mu ,
